audit.summary: The current Theorem 1 still overextends a zero-presynaptic-input gradient identity into all-weight gradient vanishing and a saddle classification. A silent-output surrogate-gradient example contradicts the broad statement, while the saddle inference lacks local geometry. Separately, the current later Python release repeats the threshold surrogate factor; the official C++ path does not. The Major label concerns the substantial theorem argument, without refuting reported SNN accuracy or sparsity.
limitations: No author code, old verifier or SNN training was executed. The original official supplement and later Python release are distinct implementations. The input-layer convention affects the scope of the silent-output counterexample, and ordinary hard-forward derivatives are kept separate from surrogate updates. Performance and energy effects remain unmeasured.

proposition.claim:
Theorem 1 argues that a silent layer causes all-weight zero gradients and a saddle point.

Eq. (\(13\)) gives threshold derivative \(-g\), where \(g\) is the triangular surrogate.
